## Dropship for SteamOS 0.1.0 — pre-release

An early build of the SteamOS server selector. One archive, one command.

**Verified on a real Steam Deck:** the nftables/cgroup-v2 blocking mechanism; the manual
Apply and Disable path in the app; the installer, the launcher entry and the uninstall
round trip; and the watcher service applying blocks on launch and removing them on exit —
the last of these driven against a stand-in process shaped exactly like Steam's game scope,
not against Overwatch itself.

**Not yet verified:** a real Overwatch launch driving the automatic path end to end. The
stand-in imitates the cgroup faithfully, but it is not the game. If the rules do not appear
within about ten seconds of a real launch, that is the known gap — the manual Apply path in
the app is the fallback, and it is unaffected.

### Install

```sh
tar -xzf dropship-steamos-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd dropship-steamos-0.1.0
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
sudo ./install.sh
```

That installs the privileged helper, the watcher service and a **Dropship for SteamOS**
entry in the application launcher. Open it, choose your regions, and switch on **Block while
Overwatch runs**. Remove everything again with `sudo ./install.sh --uninstall`.

Requires x86_64 SteamOS. Built on Ubuntu 24.04, which is older than the Deck's glibc — so
nothing newer than what the Deck already has is required. The binaries are dynamically
linked against glibc, so they are not portable to musl distributions.

This release is marked a **pre-release**, so it will not appear under "Latest" on the
releases page. That is deliberate: it becomes a normal release once a real Overwatch launch
has driven the automatic path on hardware.
